universalAnswers.whatHappened: Google announced two live voice models September 15 and begins consumer rollout.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: Models are trained components behind responses; these models serve live voice conversations.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Actual dated Google blog body and both complete primary model documentation captures.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Provider documentation shows intended capabilities, not independent task reliability or individual account availability.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A reader can change a personal planning constraint while discussing it aloud.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Search Live and Gemini Live users as rollout proceeds; Workspace eligibility varies by Google AI subscription.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Consumer rollout begins; Docs Pro/Ultra and Gmail/Keep all Google AI subscribers are announced boundaries.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Exact account timing and success on a real personal task were not tested.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Try a harmless day-trip outline, alter one constraint and inspect the final plan.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What actual result shows the request finished and the constraint was respected?

model-tool-release.productRange: Gemini 3.8 Live for quicker dialogue and Extended Thinking for multi-step live voice tasks.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: Background processing can continue during speech instead of speech completion indicating an idle system.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Back-and-forth personal planning with changed constraints or live troubleshooting discussions.
model-tool-release.notFor: A routine email or one-line question may be adequately served by existing typed chat.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: 3.8 Live is the documented quick-dialogue default; Extended Thinking targets heavier reasoning; typed chat suits a simple ask.
model-tool-release.availability: Google announces rollout in Search Live/Gemini Live and specific Workspace subscription categories.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: Docs requires Google AI Pro or Ultra; Gmail/Keep eligibility covers all Google AI subscribers.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: Paid-plan boundaries disclosed without prices or a purchase recommendation; no exact usage allowance inferred.
model-tool-release.limitations: Rollout wording does not prove a specific account has access; continuous speech does not prove completion or accuracy.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: Developer turn/idle distinction is translated into a spoken-reply/result distinction, without code or protocol names.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: Google states design/rollout; LAiDIES interprets how a reader can test a harmless personal example.
